title: Reliability, Observability & Production Engineering
summary: Measure, operate and improve production systems using observability, SLOs, capacity models, incident response, load testing and fault injection.

modules.title: Observability model & telemetry architecture
modules.summary: Know what questions logs, metrics, traces and profiles answer and how context joins them.
modules.why: Telemetry volume is useless unless it lets engineers infer internal state from external evidence.

units.title: Logs, metrics, traces, profiles & events
units.summary: Choose the right telemetry signal for each diagnostic question.
units.challenge: Map ten production questions to the minimum telemetry needed to answer them.
units.evidence: Signal-selection matrix with cost/cardinality notes.

units.title: Correlation, trace context & causal stitching
units.summary: Carry request/work identifiers across async and service boundaries.
units.challenge: Trace a frontend→API→queue→worker workflow end-to-end.
units.evidence: Telemetry screenshots/logs joined by shared context.

units.title: Telemetry collection, sampling & backend architecture
units.summary: Move telemetry reliably without making observability itself the outage.
units.challenge: Design telemetry for 500 services under budget/cardinality constraints.
units.evidence: Pipeline architecture and sampling/retention policy.

modules.title: Production logging & audit-quality events
modules.summary: Create structured, useful and safe logs rather than unsearchable text dumps.
modules.why: Logs are often the only detailed evidence after a failure, but can leak data and explode cost.

units.title: Structured logging & event design
units.summary: Log stable fields and meaningful events rather than interpolated prose only.
units.challenge: Replace ad-hoc logs in one feature with an event-oriented schema.
units.evidence: Before/after searchability and sample queries.

units.title: Log levels, volume & sensitive-data controls
units.summary: Keep logs useful without leaking secrets or creating unaffordable volume.
units.challenge: Audit a noisy service and reduce volume while preserving incident evidence.
units.evidence: Log-volume/cost before and after plus redaction tests.

units.title: Log-based investigation & timeline reconstruction
units.summary: Reconstruct multi-service failure timelines from structured events.
units.challenge: Diagnose a seeded cross-service failure using logs only.
units.evidence: Incident timeline citing exact evidence.

modules.title: Metrics, histograms & dimensionality
modules.summary: Measure rates, levels, distributions and saturation with controlled cardinality.
modules.why: Bad metrics produce beautiful dashboards that cannot answer operational questions.

units.title: Counters, gauges, histograms & labels
units.summary: Represent measurements with correct aggregation semantics.
units.challenge: Instrument request, queue and worker metrics and justify each type/label.
units.evidence: Metric catalog and sample queries.

units.title: Latency distributions & percentiles
units.summary: Understand p50/p95/p99 and why averages hide tail pain.
units.challenge: Generate bimodal latency and compare average vs percentile interpretation.
units.evidence: Latency report explaining user cohorts hidden by mean.

units.title: Cardinality, cost & dimensional design
units.summary: Avoid labels that create unbounded time-series explosion.
units.challenge: Redesign a per-user metric into bounded aggregate + trace/log drilldown.
units.evidence: Estimated series count before/after.

modules.title: Distributed tracing & latency decomposition
modules.summary: Follow requests across services, queues and databases to locate critical-path latency and errors.
modules.why: Microservice latency is composed across boundaries; local service dashboards cannot show the whole path.

units.title: Spans, parenting & attributes
units.summary: Represent units of work and their causal hierarchy.
units.challenge: Instrument HTTP + DB + outbound call spans and inspect critical path.
units.evidence: Trace screenshot with latency breakdown.

units.title: Async/message tracing & links
units.summary: Propagate causality through queues where timing/parent structure differs from synchronous calls.
units.challenge: Trace one published event consumed by three independent services.
units.evidence: Trace model explaining parent/link choices.

units.title: Trace sampling & retention strategy
units.summary: Preserve rare/failing requests without tracing every byte forever.
units.challenge: Design sampling for high-QPS service while retaining slow/error traces.
units.evidence: Sampling policy and expected storage rate.

modules.title: Profiling & runtime performance telemetry
modules.summary: Use CPU/allocation/lock profiles to find code-level bottlenecks in production-like workloads.
modules.why: Metrics tell you something is slow; profiles reveal where resources are consumed.

units.title: CPU & allocation profiles
units.summary: Find hot methods and allocation pressure using sampling/profiling tools.
units.challenge: Identify a CPU or allocation hotspot in a loaded Java endpoint.
units.evidence: Profile before/after code change with measured impact.

units.title: Lock, blocking & off-CPU analysis
units.summary: Find time lost waiting rather than computing.
units.challenge: Diagnose a latency spike caused by synchronized contention or pool wait.
units.evidence: Thread/profile evidence connecting wait state to latency.

units.title: Production profiling overhead & methodology
units.summary: Collect useful profiles without perturbing the system or misreading samples.
units.challenge: Write a safe production profiling runbook.
units.evidence: Methodology with guardrails and stop conditions.

modules.title: SLIs, SLOs, SLAs & error budgets
modules.summary: Turn reliability from vague aspiration into measurable product objectives.
modules.why: Without explicit objectives teams either over-engineer everything or discover reliability expectations during incidents.

units.title: User-journey SLIs
units.summary: Measure availability/latency/correctness at boundaries users actually experience.
units.challenge: Define SLIs for login, task edit and notification delivery.
units.evidence: SLI specification including numerator/denominator/data source.

units.title: SLO targets, windows & multi-window thinking
units.summary: Choose targets/windows that match product expectations and release/incident decisions.
units.challenge: Set defensible SLOs for free vs enterprise tenant tiers.
units.evidence: Target rationale tied to product impact/cost.

units.title: Error budgets & reliability policy
units.summary: Use allowed unreliability to balance feature velocity and reliability work.
units.challenge: Create an error-budget policy for a team that repeatedly breaches SLO after releases.
units.evidence: Policy with release/reliability actions at budget thresholds.

modules.title: Alerting, on-call & operational response
modules.summary: Page humans only for actionable user-impacting conditions and provide fast context.
modules.why: Bad alerting burns engineers and still misses real incidents.

units.title: Symptom-based vs cause-based alerts
units.summary: Page on user impact while using cause signals for diagnosis.
units.challenge: Replace CPU/instance alerts with service-level symptom alerts and supporting diagnostics.
units.evidence: Alert catalog with action owner/runbook.

units.title: SLO burn-rate alerting
units.summary: Detect fast and slow reliability budget consumption across windows.
units.challenge: Calculate burn for simulated incidents and define page/ticket thresholds.
units.evidence: Alert formulas and incident examples.

units.title: On-call design, runbooks & escalation
units.summary: Make response roles, access and diagnostics predictable under stress.
units.challenge: Create an on-call package for the capstone including first-10-minute checklist.
units.evidence: Runbook and escalation tree tested in a drill.

modules.title: Incident command, diagnosis & postmortems
modules.summary: Coordinate technical response while preserving communication and learning.
modules.why: Severe incidents are socio-technical coordination problems, not only debugging sessions.

units.title: Incident roles, command & communication
units.summary: Separate incident coordination, technical work and stakeholder communication.
units.challenge: Run a timed tabletop outage with assigned roles.
units.evidence: Incident timeline/status updates and role retrospective.

units.title: Mitigation, stabilization & root cause
units.summary: Restore service before over-optimizing diagnosis when safe.
units.challenge: Given ambiguous evidence, choose reversible mitigations before full diagnosis.
units.evidence: Decision log explaining risk of each mitigation.

units.title: Blameless postmortems & systemic follow-up
units.summary: Turn incidents into improved controls, designs and organizational learning.
units.challenge: Write a postmortem for a simulated cascade/retry outage.
units.evidence: Postmortem with prioritized prevention/detection/mitigation actions.

modules.title: Capacity planning, queueing & saturation
modules.summary: Predict throughput/latency limits quantitatively before production discovers them.
modules.why: Systems fail at bottlenecks; capacity reasoning connects workload demand to constrained resources.

units.title: Workload & demand modeling
units.summary: Describe traffic with QPS, concurrency, payload and read/write distributions.
units.challenge: Build a workload model for 1M DAU collaboration product.
units.evidence: Assumption table and peak demand calculations.

units.title: Little's Law & queue intuition
units.summary: Relate concurrency, throughput and latency and recognize waiting amplification near saturation.
units.challenge: Predict required concurrency from rate/latency and validate against load test.
units.evidence: Calculation vs observed concurrency/queue depth.

units.title: Bottleneck & capacity models
units.summary: Find limiting resource and estimate safe capacity/headroom.
units.challenge: Estimate service capacity from one constrained DB pool/CPU and validate under load.
units.evidence: Capacity model with first saturation point and scale plan.

modules.title: Load, stress, spike & soak testing
modules.summary: Use controlled workload experiments to validate capacity, latency and stability assumptions.
modules.why: A single throughput benchmark does not reveal overload behaviour, leaks or recovery.

units.title: Representative load-test design
units.summary: Generate realistic traffic mixes and measure the right service objectives.
units.challenge: Create a representative API workload from the capacity model.
units.evidence: Test plan linking workload assumptions to generated traffic.

units.title: Stress, spike & recovery behaviour
units.summary: Push beyond capacity and observe failure/recovery shape.
units.challenge: Exceed service capacity then remove load; verify it recovers without restart/backlog collapse.
units.evidence: Throughput/latency/error/queue graphs across overload and recovery.

units.title: Soak testing & slow degradation
units.summary: Find leaks, fragmentation, queue drift and connection lifecycle problems over time.
units.challenge: Run sustained load long enough to detect a seeded resource leak.
units.evidence: Time-series evidence and leak root cause.

modules.title: Fault injection & chaos engineering
modules.summary: Validate resilience assumptions by causing controlled failures before incidents do.
modules.why: Resilience patterns are hypotheses until tested under realistic failure timing and combinations.

units.title: Latency, errors, crashes & dependency faults
units.summary: Inject specific failure modes with bounded blast radius.
units.challenge: Run a controlled dependency-latency experiment and validate timeout/circuit behaviour.
units.evidence: Hypothesis, experiment, observed deviation and fix.

units.title: Chaos experiment design & safety
units.summary: Define steady state, scope, abort conditions and learning goals.
units.challenge: Design a production-safe node-loss experiment.
units.evidence: Experiment plan with abort metrics and expected learning.

units.title: Cross-system game days
units.summary: Exercise technical and human response to compound failures.
units.challenge: Run tabletop: primary DB failover plus retry storm plus stale cache.
units.evidence: Game-day report and architecture changes.

modules.title: Availability, redundancy & durability engineering
modules.summary: Design redundancy based on correlated failures and user-visible service objectives.
modules.why: Adding replicas does not help if they share the same failure domain or operational dependency.

units.title: Availability composition & dependency chains
units.summary: Estimate system availability from serial/parallel dependencies and redundancy assumptions.
units.challenge: Estimate a service objective across auth, API and database dependencies.
units.evidence: Availability model and biggest risk contributors.

units.title: Redundancy across failure domains
units.summary: Place copies so common failures do not remove all capacity.
units.challenge: Review an apparently replicated system with hidden shared dependencies.
units.evidence: Failure-domain diagram and remediation.

units.title: Durability, corruption & data integrity
units.summary: Protect against deletion/corruption as well as hardware loss.
units.challenge: Design defense against accidental mass deletion replicated to every region.
units.evidence: Data protection layers and recovery path.

modules.title: Disaster recovery & backup operations
modules.summary: Set and test RPO/RTO for realistic disaster scenarios, not only infrastructure loss.
modules.why: DR plans fail when dependencies, credentials, DNS, data and human procedures are never exercised together.

units.title: RPO/RTO by disaster scenario
units.summary: Define acceptable data loss/recovery time for regional loss, corruption and operator mistakes.
units.challenge: Set different RPO/RTO for comments, payments/audit and analytics data.
units.evidence: Recovery objective table with business rationale.

units.title: Backup verification & restore drills
units.summary: Continuously prove backups are usable and complete.
units.challenge: Restore a fresh environment from backup and compare invariants/counts.
units.evidence: Restore report with measured RTO and validation queries.

units.title: DR runbooks, automation & failback
units.summary: Make recovery repeatable and prevent rushed failback from causing a second incident.
units.challenge: Write and tabletop a full regional failover/failback procedure.
units.evidence: Timed runbook with decision points and owners.

modules.title: Production debugging & evidence-driven diagnosis
modules.summary: Move from symptom to constrained component and root cause across app/runtime/network/data layers.
modules.why: Senior engineers are valuable when they can make progress under incomplete, noisy production evidence.

units.title: Triage: scope, change, saturation & dependency
units.summary: Reduce the search space quickly before deep-diving one theory.
units.challenge: Given an unknown latency incident, create first-15-minute investigation sequence.
units.evidence: Triage decision tree and evidence gathered.

units.title: Cross-layer diagnosis
units.summary: Correlate application, JVM, DB, network and infrastructure evidence.
units.challenge: Diagnose a seeded issue whose symptom appears in API but root cause is lower layer.
units.evidence: Evidence chain with rejected hypotheses.

units.title: Safe diagnostics in production
units.summary: Collect evidence and mitigate without adding load or destroying forensic state.
units.challenge: Choose safe diagnostics for overloaded production DB/JVM under strict SLO pressure.
units.evidence: Investigation/mitigation plan ordered by risk.

modules.title: Toil reduction & operational excellence
modules.summary: Turn repeated manual operational work into safe automation and clearer ownership.
modules.why: Reliable teams improve systems so the same incident/manual task does not recur indefinitely.

units.title: Toil identification & prioritization
units.summary: Recognize repetitive manual operational work that scales with service growth.
units.challenge: Inventory operational tasks and rank automation opportunities.
units.evidence: Toil backlog with quantified monthly cost.

units.title: Safe operational automation
units.summary: Automate with idempotency, previews, limits and rollback rather than brittle scripts.
units.challenge: Automate a batch repair/maintenance task with guardrails.
units.evidence: Automation safety checklist and failure tests.

units.title: Operational readiness reviews
units.summary: Verify a service is supportable before launch.
units.challenge: Conduct an operational readiness review for a new service.
units.evidence: Readiness checklist with blocking vs follow-up findings.
